name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in Georgia
Jasmine Clark's $2.3 million raised and $4.2 million in outside support versus no visible Republican fundraising
Prediction markets price Democrats at about 97 percent to hold the seat
Open seat with no general-election polling creates residual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+21 lean, Clark's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent for Democrats all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat and absence of polling.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or unusually low Democratic turnout in this low-profile open seat could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is among the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points. The open-seat contest pits Jasmine Clark, who emerged from a competitive Democratic primary, against Republican Jonathan Chavez. No general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing.

Clark has raised about $2.3 million and drawn more than $4 million in outside support, while Chavez shows no measurable fundraising footprint. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat. With the district's heavy Democratic lean and the stark resource imbalance, Democrats are strong favorites to keep this seat, though the lack of polling and the open-seat dynamic leave some residual uncertainty.
